definitions.name: Alternative systems
definitions.statement: A∈R^{m×n}, b∈R^m with ||b||≠0; one fixed ρ>0. X={x≥0:Ax=b}, U={u:Aᵀu≤0,bᵀu=ρ}. Exactly one is nonempty.

definitions.name: Residual primal and normalized alternative residual

theorem_cards.label: Equations(1)–(6): reconstruct the minimum-norm solution of the consistent alternative
assumptions: Finite real A,b; ρ>0 fixed; exact global minimizers x* of(1) and u* of(2).
No rank assumption on A in this part; b≠0 is printed background.
theorem_cards.statement: With z*=b−Ax*, Aᵀz*≤0 and bᵀz*=||z*||². If X is empty, z*≠0 and ρz*/||z*||² is the minimum-Euclidean-norm point of U. With w1*=(Aᵀu*)+, w2*=ρ−bᵀu*, Aw1*=bw2* and ||w1*||²+w2*²=ρw2*. If X is nonempty then w2*>0 and w1*/w2* is the minimum-Euclidean-norm point of X.
proof_steps: 作者使用二次强对偶与驻点关系；原文列出残差恒等式和重构公式，但未展开所有最小范数证明。
本次局部推导：orthant KKT for(1) gives Aᵀz≤0, xᵀAᵀz=0, hence bᵀz=||z||². Projection onto the finitely generated closed cone A(R_+^n) gives, for every u∈U, ρ=bᵀu≤zᵀu≤||z||||u||; scaled z attains the bound.

本次局部推导：(2) is differentiable convex with gradient A(Aᵀu)+−b(ρ−bᵀu). Its stationary point gives Aw1=bw2. Inner product with u yields ||w1||²+w2²=ρw2, thus w2≥0. If X is feasible, w2=0 would give w1=0 and an impossible certificate u∈U; therefore w2>0.

本次局部推导：on each feasible ray (w1,w2)=(tx,t), x∈X, dual(4) has maximumρ²/[2(1+||x||²)] at t=ρ/(1+||x||²)>0. The unique strictly concave dual maximizer therefore selects the minimum-norm x, justifying(5).
gaps: Exact residual zero tests and division by nonzero residual/positive w2 are mathematical formulas, not certified floating-point stopping criteria.
Finite polyhedral-image closure ensures minimizers exist; no analogous nonclosed infinite-dimensional image claim follows.
The note cites earlier methods for computational advantage; it does not prove a rate, complexity bound, or conditioning guarantee.

theorem_cards.label: Equations(7)–(12): equivalent nullspace system and alternate matrix
assumptions: Rank(A)=m≤n, ν=n−m; choose any particular xbar with Axbar=b.
K∈R^{ν×n} has independent rows forming a basis of ker A, hence AKᵀ=0.
theorem_cards.statement: X is in affine bijection with Y={y:Kᵀy≤xbar}, through x=xbar−Kᵀy and y=(KKᵀ)^{-1}K(xbar−x). The alternative system is V={v≥0:Kv=0,−xbarᵀv=ρ}. X and Y are simultaneously feasible/infeasible; V is alternative to both. U and V are in bijection v=−Aᵀu, u=−(AAᵀ)^{-1}Av.
proof_steps: 作者证明：rankm yields all affine solutions x=xbar−Kᵀy; full column rank Kᵀ makes the inverse pseudoinverse formula valid for x in that affine fiber.
作者借用Gale alternative for Kᵀy≤xbar.

本次可自含核验：ker K=range Aᵀ under the full-row-rank hypothesis. For v=−Aᵀu, Kv=0, v≥0 iff Aᵀu≤0, and −xbarᵀv=bᵀu. Conversely full row rank makes Aᵀ injective, so the inverse is unique. This reduces the new alternative to the ordinary finite Farkas alternative already mapped in B01.
gaps: The sentence “if m≤n, Ax=b is always solvable” inherits the preceding rank(A)=m hypothesis; dimension inequality alone is insufficient.
When m=n, ν=0 there is no free y. Interpret Y as the singleton zero-dimensional coordinate if xbar≥0, otherwise empty; do not require an ordinary positive-dimensional KKᵀ inverse.
When rank(A)<m these displayed bijections/inverses fail as written; one must first reduce independent equations and check consistency.
Lower variable count ν or m is not a runtime theorem; changing the basis K can worsen conditioning.

theorem_cards.label: Primal zero-objective LP interpretation
assumptions: Finite LP P:min0ᵀx subject Ax=b,x≥0; D:max bᵀu subject Aᵀu≤0.
Use the finite LP feasibility/unboundedness duality theorem as an external foundation.
theorem_cards.statement: Since D containsu=0, either P is feasible with optimalvalue0 and all dual values≤0, or P is infeasible and D is unbounded above. Scaling a positive dual ray normalizes bᵀu to any prescribedρ>0, yielding the Farkas alternative.
proof_steps: 作者证明：exclude cases with dual infeasibility; use weak duality for the feasible branch and the finite LP duality classification for the infeasible branch.
gaps: This is a reduction to finite LP duality, not a proof independent of every theorem of alternatives.
The general four-case LP classification is cited as common knowledge; the card treats it as a foundation dependency rather than claiming a new general duality proof.

constant_dependence.explicit: ρ>0 freely normalizes the alternative certificate. Recovered ||u_normal||=ρ/||z*||. In the feasible branch w2*=ρ/(1+||x_normal||²). Nullspace inverse depends on KKᵀ and AAᵀ.
constant_dependence.dependence: Small inconsistency residual or large feasible normal norm creates division sensitivity; no finite precision or iteration guarantee is supplied.

endpoint_limits: b=0, excluded in the text, is directly feasible viax=0 and cannot have bᵀu=ρ>0.
ρ=0 would destroy exclusive alternatives becauseu=0 is always feasible; positive normalization is essential.
Only the dimension-reduction part requires full row rank.
No nonclosed conic image, arbitrary Hilbert space or center-cube theorem follows.
reusable_methods: Separate exact finite feasibility certificates from numerical residual size.
Use projection/KKT residual identities to reconstruct a normalized certificate.
Reduce a consistent affine fiber by an explicit nullspace basis while recording inverse conditioning and rank prerequisites.
